results.content:
# From Containers to Containment: Manufacturing Trust in the Agentic Era with Docker

Today, we officially unveiled a new Docker, complete with a new look, a new logo, and new tagline: Run on Trust. The agentic era has thus far proven long on possibilities and short on trust. Docker is intent on changing the latter.

If you’ve been following along, you know Docker’s transformation didn’t happen overnight. Instead, we’ve been steadily building toward it for the better part of the past year: making our catalog of more than 4,000 Docker Hardened Images (DHI) free and fully open source under the Apache 2.0 license, shipping Docker AI Governance, and launching both local and cloud sandboxes.

WeAreDevelopers Keynote [...] ### Trust comes from the system around the agent

Taken together, the announcements in my keynote form one system. Sandboxes provide a deterministic boundary. Kits make the agent’s environment and authority reproducible. Cloud Sandboxes extend the same trust model to the cloud. Developers get the freedom to choose their agents and more autonomy, while staying in control of what they can access and change.

That’s what the new Docker is all about. We spent more than a decade earning your trust with containers, and we’re building on that foundation, not replacing it, as we move from containers to containment for the agentic era.

Wherever this next chapter takes us, we’ll keep working to make Docker the place where you can run on trust.

### Ready to try Cloud Sandboxes? [...] ### An ecosystem built around trust

An open agent ecosystem needs both choice for developers and shared standards the industry can build on. Being open and ecosystem-first has always been part of who Docker is, and it’s a big part of why we believe the industry can trust us here.

Nous Research joined me onstage to show Hermes running as a first-class Kit in Docker Sandboxes: a third-party agent packaged for a common environment, with Docker providing the isolation and controls. We’ve also committed to submitting our Kits specification to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF), the open source, vendor-neutral hub of cloud-native computing. Docker provides the trusted foundation underneath, whether agents run locally or in the cloud.

results.title: Meet the New Docker: Built to Run on Trust | Docker
results.content:
## Containers weren’t designed for agents

Agents have introduced a new problem. Containers isolate workloads. But agents aren’t workloads. Agents are actors.

Agents make their own decisions about what to run, what to access, and what to change. Developers and enterprises need solutions built specifically to isolate and govern them, so they can give those agents real autonomy without giving up control.

Docker’s next chapter is about delivering exactly that: security, isolation, and governance, so we can all trust agents to do meaningful work without feeling like we’re always one step from catastrophe.

## Run on trust

In case I haven’t made it blindingly obvious yet, the new Docker is all about trust. [...] Enter a company you might have heard of: Docker.

Together with all of you, Docker built the standard trusted by millions of developers. For over a decade, developers have relied on us to make software portable, open, reproducible, and secure. Docker turned the frustration of “Well, it works on my machine!” into the assurance that “Yes, it works everywhere.”

Today, of course, the challenge confronting us is new and evolving, and we all need to evolve with it. We cannot simply continue to do what we’ve always done and expect to succeed in this new era. That applies to business leaders, developers, tech companies, everyone. It certainly applies to Docker. That’s what this rebrand is about: evolving to meet the moment for our customers.

## What isn’t changing [...] ### Evolving an iconic brand for the agentic era

Today, Docker is officially launching its new brand, and I’m excited to tell you what it’s all about and why we think now is the time for change.

Let’s start with the big picture. We’re living through a transformative moment: for Docker, for developers, for the industry, and quite possibly, for humanity itself. AI is creating possibilities that would have sounded like science fiction not long ago.

But it’s also forcing the industry to confront an almost existential question: how do we harness all that power and intelligence without compromising security, governance, or control? Or, put more simply: how do we get to a point where we can actually trust agents?

results.title: The New Docker: From Containerization to Trust in the Agentic AI Era
results.content:
The familiar Docker experience remains, but its positioning is expanding.

Traditionally, Docker has been closely associated with containerization, application portability, and consistent development environments. Now, the company is extending that story towards secure execution, AI agent isolation, and enterprise governance.

The objective is straightforward: help developers build and run applications and AI agents in environments they can trust.

## Why Is Docker Evolving?

AI agents are changing how developers interact with development environments.

Unlike traditional application workloads, autonomous agents can execute commands, access files, interact with tools, install dependencies, and perform actions based on their instructions.

This introduces new security considerations. [...] This introduces new security considerations.

A traditional container provides process isolation, but containers share the host operating system kernel. When autonomous agents are given access to development environments, credentials, files, and other resources, controlling their permissions becomes particularly important.

This is where Docker's new direction becomes interesting.

Docker is focusing on providing additional isolation and governance mechanisms specifically designed for agentic workloads.

## Three Pillars Behind the New Docker

Docker's new positioning can be understood through three important areas.

### 1. Trusted Runtime

AI agents need controlled environments in which they can execute tasks. [...] Docker has been a fundamental part of modern software development for more than a decade. From simplifying application deployment to enabling consistent development environments, containers have changed how developers build, package, ship, and run applications.

But technology never stands still.

On November 19, 2026, Docker introduced a new brand identity with a clear message: Built to Run on Trust.

This is more than a visual refresh. It represents Docker's evolving vision for a development ecosystem increasingly influenced by Artificial Intelligence (AI), autonomous agents, and security requirements.

## A New Identity, A New Direction

Docker's new identity brings a redesigned website, refreshed visual language, updated colours, and an evolved version of its familiar Moby whale.

results.content:
Today, we’re building on that foundation and extending that trust into the agentic era. At WeAreDevelopers, you saw the first steps. We launched Docker Cloud Sandboxes, published the next-generation Sandbox Kit specification (which we’ve committed to submitting to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation), and built nearly everything we showed around one idea: helping developers manufacture trust for AI agents.

If it all looked and felt like a slightly different Docker, that was intentional. We’re at the start of a transformative era for Docker, and you’ll see a lot more from us in the coming weeks and months.

But no matter how much the industry changes, and no matter how much we evolve along with it, one thing won’t change. Docker will continue to run on trust. [...] ## Why “Navigator”

AI adoption is not following a normal technology curve. Every team, every vendor, every model provider, and every hyperscaler is racing to ship agentic capability, and no single company sees the whole stack. Identity, observability, supply chain security, MCP gateways, models, and clouds are each building their piece. What enterprises are missing is a trusted, common layer that lets those pieces work together safely.

That’s Docker’s role. Docker is where agents, models, and tools actually run: vertically integrated where it matters, and horizontally open to everything our customers already use. We describe it as being the Trusted Navigator for the agentic era; the constant that helps customers make sense of a landscape moving faster than any one team can track. [...] ]]>   From Containers to Sandboxes: Developer Trust in the Agentic Era  Fri, 16 Oct 2026 16:00:00 +0000  What the 2026 Stack Overflow Developer Survey tells us about where trust goes next

If you’ve followed Docker lately, you know we’re all-in on sandboxes. We’ve spent a ton of time talking about the difference between sandboxes and containers, and helping our customers and the industry as a whole understand when to use which. In fact, Docker president Mark Cavage dedicated his opening keynote at WeAreDevelopers World Congress North America to this exact topic, using live demos to show why sandboxes (and not containers) provide the level of isolation required to contain autonomous agents.
